newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanjin to invest 75m marks in DSR-Senator.
newsitem.headline: Hanjin to invest 75m marks in DSR-Senator.

text.p: South Korea's Hanjin Shipping Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had agreed in principle to invest 75 million marks in German shipping firm DSR-Senator Lines as part of a plan to increase the company's capital by 100 million marks.

A spokesman for Hanjin Shipping, a unit of the Hanjin Group, said the planned investment was agreed when it signed a memorandum of understanding last week to become the majority shareholder in the German shipping firm.
"It's still an agreement in principle and the deal has yet to be finalised," said the spokesman. He did not say when the finalised contract could be made.
He said the memorandum also stipulated that Hanjin would hold about two thirds of the German firm's enlarged capital.
Hanjin said last week the DSR-Senator fleet would continue to operate totally independently from Hanjin.
The company also has said the DSR-Senator fleet would consist of about 30 ships with a carrying capacity of about 100,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) by 1998.
DSR-Senator is currently owned by Deutsche Seereederei, Hanseatische Industriebeteiligungen and Commercium.
